subject.title: WhatsApp 1:1: inbound image wedges main lane ~3min before processing — multimodal run strands active_reply_work/queued_work_without_active_run (repro on 2026.6.10, post-#95039)

question: Should this focused WhatsApp image `active_reply_work` variant stay as its own tracker, fold into the broader WhatsApp lane tracker, or wait for a fresh current-main live repro before code work?
rationale: The code path is real, but the fix changes session recovery policy where the tradeoff is between releasing stale reply ownership promptly and avoiding aborts of legitimate active runs.

options.title: Sponsor focused active-reply fix
options.body: Keep this issue open for a narrow fix to active reply-work cleanup/recovery, while linking the broader WhatsApp tracker as related background.

options.title: Fold into broad tracker
options.body: Close this as covered by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97538 only if maintainers want one WhatsApp lane-recovery tracker despite the image-specific trigger.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Keep implementation paused until a current-main WhatsApp image burst repro proves whether b1da-adjacent recovery changes altered the observed loop.

recommendation.title: Sponsor focused active-reply fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a narrow fix to active reply-work cleanup/recovery, while linking the broader WhatsApp tracker as related background.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior scoping comments and the related follow-up-drain fix make this the strongest available routing signal for the recovery-policy decision.
